text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
24 CHASA

-- Bulgaria's debt-ridden National Electricity Company has some 200 million levs blocked in banks, which the central bank put under special supervision on Monday, the company's director Kozma Kuzmanov said.

-- Budget-funded enterprises serviced by banks under special superivision, will have to transfer their account into Bulbank, Biochim, Expressbank, United Bulgarian Bank, Bulgarian Post Bank or Hebrosbank, the central bank said.

-- Bulgaria's second largest credit institution, the State Savings Bank said it will offer between 22 and 25 percent monthly interest on citizens' and firms' lev deposits up to 12 months from Monday in line with the new central interest rate of 300 percent annually.
STANDART
-- Salary payments in state companies funded by the budget were delayed after the Bulgarian National Bank put nine more banks under special supervision, a central bank official said.

-- Bulgaria may face power cuts this winter if the oldest Soviet-made reactor at the Kozloduy nuclear power plant, which has started safety tests is not connected to the national grid, by December, the National Electricity Company's chairman said.

-- Socialist party deputies in parliament demanded an investigation of incollateralised credits extended by the nine banks placed under special supervision on Monday to find the culprits for the grave financial condition of those banks.
KONTINENT

-- Bulgaria's parliament budget committee decided that citizens' deposits in the nine banks put under special supervision will be 100 percent guaranteed by the state immediately after the central bank's decisison.
The decisison overruled a Socialist cabinet proposal to pay individuals' deposits only after the court rules on banks' insolvency.
-- Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov and central bank board member Zdravko Balyozov left for Washington to participate in the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
PARI

-- Bulgaria's minimum limit for a foreign investment is expected to be set at $50,000 and foreigners' deposit accounts in local banks will not be recognised as investments under amendments to the Foreign Investment Law tentatively approved by the parliament.

-- Interbank settlements for a total of 20 billion levs have been delayed since Monday when the central bank put nine banks under special supervision because most of them could not meet outstanding payments, central bank officials said.
TRUD

-- Bulgaria's Chief Prosecutor's Office and Interior Ministry have banned bankers from the nine banks placed under special supervision from leaving the country, the chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev said.
-- Bulgaria's government is expected to raise cigarette and fuel prices for October by 20 percent on the average, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
